pairs.difference: A: the hearse body carries streaky painted reflections on black paint, with wobbly gold trim and chrome and hard specular strokes on nearly every part. Detail, micro-texture and gloss (0.317) are all above the real range. B: the boat and pier planks are plain satin wood with quiet line grain, and the rope twist is fine. All B's measures are in range.
pairs.fix: Keep the black body a soft satin with one broad, smooth reflection; remove the small painted streaks on the fenders and doors; keep chrome only on the grille and bumper, with the gold trim thin and matte.

pairs.difference: A: the beach ball is soft vinyl with thin raised seams and one blurred highlight. It is very low on detail, but that suits a plain object and matches the softness of the real computer and glove. B: the pumpkin bucket and every candy share one saturated lacquer, with hot highlights on each candy and chunky toy wrapper folds. The evidence is weak because A's numbers fall below the real range while B's are in range.
pairs.fix: Make the bucket a duller moulded plastic with a broad, soft sheen; keep shine only on the candy wrappers, and make their folds smaller and thinner.

pairs.difference: A: the map has hard inked outlines on flat colour with no paper fibre or soft creases, and the magnifier rim has sharp painted bands. Detail, micro-texture and highlight are above range. B: the cap matches the real reference, with a fine weave on the navy band, a matte white crown, a satin visor and a small polished button.
pairs.fix: Draw the map as soft matte paper with faint fold shading and thin, quiet printed lines; give the magnifier rim one smooth metal gradient instead of painted bands.

pairs.difference: A: the chest has large decorative wood grain, knots and cracks in dark painted strokes, with chunky rivets and a toy-like, lacquered gold padlock. B: the pink tray has soft silicone sheen and translucent ice, though the frost crust is speckled. Measures do not separate them, so this rests on the oversized grain and painted marks on A.
pairs.fix: Make the wood grain fine and faint with no big knots or cracks; make the rivets smaller and the iron bands a dull matte; give the padlock a single soft highlight.

pairs.difference: B: the purple cover has an all-over pebbled leather grain, dashed stitching and hard gold corners with rivets. This added micro-detail matches the dashed stitches and pebbled grips on the generated gloves and cameras. A: the teal cover is plain satin with crisp sticker shapes, closer to the real plain surfaces, although the wood grain behind it is coarse. Measures are close, with B lower.
pairs.fix: Smooth the cover to a soft, faintly grained leather with a low sheen; make the stitching barely visible; soften the gold corners into satin metal with smaller rivets.

pairs.difference: A: the flask has hard painted glass streaks, pearlescent bubbles with rainbow rims and a speckled cork, so fine ornamental detail sits on glossy surfaces. B: the bottle is frosted, translucent plastic with soft transitions and one quiet sheen, like the soft real finish, though its detail is near the bottom of the real range.
pairs.fix: Use clear glass with one soft window highlight and a faint rim line; make the bubbles plain and small with no rainbow edges; give the cork a smooth matte face.

pairs.difference: A: the skull is one material throughout, soft clay-like plaster with almost no gloss (0.014, below range) and broad bright areas (highlight 0.28, above range). This resembles the clay finish of the generated computers. B: the shoes mix mesh, rubber and laces, but the laces and beads are chunky, the soles lacquered and the mesh noisy, so B is not clean either. B's measures stay in range.
pairs.fix: Give the bone a slightly waxy satin sheen with a soft highlight on the brow and cheek; add faint, fine pores; make the teeth a little glossier than the skull; make the orange paint a thin painted layer.

pairs.difference: B: the bat's body and wings carry mottled speckle and fuzzy painted noise, so skin, fur and membrane read as one grainy surface. A: the wristband is clean silicone with smooth tone and crisp raised icons, matching the smooth finish of the real cards. Both are in range, so this rests on the visible noise.
pairs.fix: Remove the speckled noise; make the body short, soft velvet fur, and the wings a smooth thin matte skin with a faint sheen along the bones.

pairs.difference: B: the web reads as white plastic tubing with bulb joints and grey rods, not silk, and the single droplet is a toy bead. Highlight share is 0.291, above range. A: the whistle is one satin moulded plastic with a dull metal ring and soft edges, close to the real finish, although its gloss is very low.
pairs.fix: Draw the web as thin, fine, slightly translucent silk threads with no knobs at the joints, with tiny dew drops catching light.

pairs.difference: B: every topiary leaf is an equally lacquered, repeated chunky shape with its own highlight. Gloss (0.437), detail and micro-texture all exceed the real range. A: the tree bark uses large decorative flowing lines, which is not ideal, but it stays matte and in range.
pairs.fix: Make the leaves much smaller and mostly matte, massed into soft clumps; let only a few top leaves catch a gentle sheen.

pairs.difference: B: the flower petals are inflated, candy-like lacquer blobs, and leaves and bricks share the same sheen, so one plastic covers everything with chunky toy detail. A: the balloons are smooth latex with one soft window highlight, like the soft real cards, although A measures below the real range on detail and gloss. The evidence is mixed.
pairs.fix: Make the petals thin and matte with soft folds, keep the leaves satin, and make the edging bricks dry rough stone with no sheen.

pairs.difference: A: the door has streaky painted brush marks, a lacquered blue surface and busy glossy ivy and flowers. Gloss (0.51), detail and micro-texture are far above range. B: the castle has matte stone with quiet block shading and fine plank lines on the door, and stays in range.
pairs.fix: Paint the door a calm satin blue with no brush streaks; make the ivy leaves matte and smaller; add gloss only on the door handle and a few petals.

pattern: Generated cards spread one treatment over the whole object: either uniform lacquer with a highlight on every small part, or a single clay-like matte. Real cards keep a soft satin base and put shine in only one or two places. Generated cards also add decorative surface marks at the wrong scale, such as big wood grain, painted brush streaks, speckled noise, and dashed stitches or pebbled grain, and they enlarge small parts into chunky toy details. Real cards keep such texture fine and quiet, or leave it out.
